key_insight: Adding ADR-based PV physics to TSMixer yielded no consistent forecasting advantage over the purely data-driven baseline.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale day-ahead PV forecasting, explicit physics integration may add complexity without reliably improving accuracy, geographic transferability, or data efficiency.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer.
Build hybrid architectures using feature augmentation and residual learning.
Compare convergence, accuracy, geographic transferability, and limited-data performance.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries; hybrids appeared to converge slightly faster but showed no consistent test-performance gains.
watch_item: The findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids and do not establish that other physics-informed approaches offer no benefit.
paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
